title: MMSearch-Plus: Benchmarking Provenance-Aware Search for Multimodal Browsing Agents
claim: Answering without search or with whole-image search fails; iterative cropping and targeted search extract fine-grained cues and reach the correct answer.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right; ✗ ✗ ✓ outcomes, rightmost panel is a two-round flowchart
description: Three dashed panels compare reasoning paradigms for one visual question. A concert image with a sign, a slogan and a singer appears at top left, with the question 'What was the performance time of the singer in this event?'. Panel 1, 'Without Search', shows a robot guessing 'Taylor Swift's Reputation Tour, May 2018', in a red answer box with a red ✗. Panel 2, 'Whole Image Search Only', shows the full image going to a retrieved webpage summary and thumbnail. The robot picks result #1, giving 'Singer A's concert in June 2024', also marked ✗. Panel 3, the 'MMSearch+ Agentic Framework', is a vertical flowchart in two rounds. Each round zooms in with scissors on the lyrics and then the singer, runs text and image searches in yellow boxes, and compares the results. It ends in a green box, 'Singer B's concert in March 2025', with a green ✓. The eye goes to the large right-hand panel.
caption: Three multimodal reasoning paradigms: 1) Without search: an MLLM answers a visual question using internal knowledge only; 2) Whole-image search: an MLLM leverages external search results retrieved from the full VQA image; 3) MMSearch-Plus agentic framework: an MLLM freely calls visual tools (cropping, OCR) and search engines to extract fine-grained cues and perform precision search. A real example is shown in Figure [ref].
abstract: Existing multimodal browsing benchmarks often fail to require genuine multimodal reasoning, as many tasks can be solved with text-only heuristics without vision-in-the-loop verification. We introduce MMSearch-Plus, a 311-task benchmark that enforces multimodal understanding by requiring extraction and propagation of fine-grained visual cues through iterative image-text retrieval and cross-validation under retrieval noise. Our curation procedure seeds questions whose answers require extrapolating from spatial cues and temporal traces to out-of-image facts such as events, dates, and venues. Beyond the dataset, we provide a model-agnostic agent framework with standard browsing tools and a set-of-mark (SoM) module, which lets the agent place marks, crop subregions, and launch targeted image/text searches. SoM enables provenance-aware zoom-and-retrieve and improves robustness in multi-step reasoning. We evaluated closed- and open-source MLLMs in this framework. The strongest system achieves an end-to-end accuracy of 36.0%, and integrating SoM produces consistent gains in multiple settings, with improvements up to +3.9 points. From failure analysis, we observe recurring errors in locating relevant webpages and distinguishing between visually similar events. These results underscore the challenges of real-world multimodal search and establish MMSearch-Plus as a rigorous benchmark for advancing agentic MLLMs.
